reason: The text demonstrates the opposite of the statement. Throughout this passage from Exodus 1-7, God explicitly affirms His covenant commitment to the Israelites. Key evidence: (1) God 'remembers' (וַיִּזְכֹּ֤ר) His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; (2) God hears the groans of the people and responds with compassion; (3) God declares He will 'take you for me as a people' (לָקַחְתִּ֨י אֶתְכֶ֥ם לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם) and 'be to you as God' (וְהָיִ֥יתִי לָכֶ֖ם לֵֽאלֹהִ֑ים); and (4) God establishes His covenant (בְּרִיתִי) with them to give them the land of Canaan. The passage shows God honoring His obligations and commitments, not disavowing loyalty or considering replacement. There is no mention of replacing the Israelites with another people in this text.
